title: micro-probe-sprint-digest (personal)
content:
Purpose: scratch capture for ~10–15min micro-runs during probe sprint. Not a formal experiment repo; keep light, fast capture.

Legend: p50/p95 latency in ms, cost = estimated $ per 1k output tokens, score = quick QA pass (0-10), qcfg = quantization config shorthand.

RUN TABLE (CSV-like)
run_id,prompt_variant,model,qcfg,batch_size,tokens_out,p50_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1k_usd,score,notes
mps-001,baseline-open-ended,gptx-7b,none,1,120,45,110,0.24,6,short answer, soft stop at 90 tokens -> sometimes truncates intent
mps-002,add-leading-system,gptx-7b,none,1,140,48,115,0.28,7,leading system phrase improves instruction following
mps-003,concise-prefix,gptx-7b,int8,1,110,38,86,0.12,6.5,int8 looks fine p50 down, p95 improved
mps-004,temperature-0.2,gptx-7b,int8,1,95,35,78,0.10,6,more deterministic but sometimes too terse
mps-005,split-chunking,gptx-7b,int8,4,320,62,150,0.18,7.5,batching 4 increases throughput, latency tail worse occasionally
mps-006,kv-cache-on,gptx-7b,int8,2,210,50,120,0.14,8,cache hit reduces repeated context cost, quality stable
mps-007,rerank-lite,gptx-7b,int8,1,130,55,130,0.16,8.2,cheap rerank (cosine on embeddings) helps ordering
mps-008,soft-prompt-1,gptx-2.7b,int8,1,100,28,70,0.06,5.5,smaller model fast but quality drop on nuanced Qs

Quick Observations:
- int8 qcfg gives ~40% cost reduction in this set with small effect on p50; p95 variable.
- batching helps throughput but increases p95; for user-perceived latency prefer batch_size=1 or 2 for interactive.
- leading-system prefix reduced clarification loops for these prompts.
- KV cache is super helpful for multi-turn emulation runs (mps-006).

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Run same prompt set on quantized 4-bit to compare quality vs int8 (target next 2 sessions).
- [ ] Add a tiny eval harness to produce automatic BLEU/rouge-like number for ranking prompts (low priority).
- [ ] Try a small reranking model hosted on tiny endpoint to see p95 impact when combined.

Notes to self (shorthand):
- If p95 > 120ms for interactive demos, default fallback to smaller model or reduce batch to 1.
- Cost calc = (tokens_out/1000) * price_reference; use price_reference from team sheet (link local).
- Capture example failure outputs in GH gist and reference in run row if needed.

Scratch ideas:
- ephemeral "probe" tag in Redwood console that routes to low-cost pool (would be nice for quick dev loops).
- tiny A/B where routing toggles between int8 and fp16 to watch real user-facing diffs.

Context links and references:
- quick test harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-sweep/pull/312
- related ticket: PROJ-487 (prompt-sweep fast-probes)

End of sheet — throwaway / iterative. Keep it short next time.
